''''' Colored Symmetry''''' is a book by [[Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov|A.V. Shubnikov]] and [[Nikolay Belov (geochemist)|N.V. Belov]] and published by [[Pergamon Press]] in 1964. The book contains translations of materials originally written in Russian and published between 1951 and 1958. The book was notable because it gave English-language speakers access to new work in the fields of  [[Dichromatic symmetry|dichromatic]] and [[polychromatic symmetry]].

==Structure and topics==
The book is divided into two parts. The first part is a translation into English of A.V. Shubnikov's book ''Symmetry and antisymmetry of finite figures'' (Russian: Симметрия и антисимметрия конечных фигур) originally published in 1951.<ref name=Shubnikov>{{cite book
	| last1 = Shubnikov
	| first1 = A.V.
	| author-link = Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov
	| date = 1951
	| title = Symmetry and antisymmetry of finite figures
	| url = 
    | url-access = 
    | language = Russian
	| location = Moscow
	| publisher = Soviet Academy of Sciences (Изд-во Академии наук СССР)
	| page = 171
	| isbn = 
    | oclc = 10804627
}}</ref> As the editor says in his preface, this book rekindled interest in the field of [[Dichromatic symmetry|antisymmetry]] after a break of 20 years.  The book defines symmetry elements, operations and groups; it then introduces the concept of antisymmetry, and derives the full set of [[Magnetic space group#Magnetic point groups|dichromatic three-dimensional point groups]]. ==Audience==

The book is written for crystallographers, mathematicians and physics researchers who are interested in the application of color symmetry to [[crystal structure]] analysis and physics experiments involving [[Magnetism|magnetic]] or [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectric]] materials.

==Reception==
The book had a mixed reception from reviewers. Allen Nussbaum in ''[[American Scientist]]'' praised the editor for constructing a consistent story from the original works, but criticised the papers in part two for being difficult to read.<ref name=Nussbaum>{{cite journal
	| last1 = Nussbaum
	| first1 = Allen
    | author-link = 
	| date = 1965
	| title = Colored symmetry
	| url = 
	| journal = [[American Scientist]]
	| volume = 53
	| issue = 1
	| pages = 66A, 68A
    | jstor = 27835909
	| doi = 
	| access-date =
}}</ref> G.S. Pawley in a review for ''Science Progress'' gave credit to the editor for adding the international notation next to the authors' "retrograde personal notation". However, he criticised claims that the book is a "valuable reference book" as being "optimistic".<ref name=Pawley>{{cite journal
	| last1 = Pawley
	| first1 = G.S.
    | author-link = 
	| date = 1965
	| title = Colored symmetry
	| url = 
	| journal = Science Progress
	| volume = 53
	| issue = 211
	| pages = 467–468
    | jstor = 43419383
	| doi = 
	| access-date =
}}</ref> [[Martin Julian Buerger|Martin Buerger]] in an extensive review for ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' also offered both praise and criticism. He stated that previous work in the field by [[William Barlow (geologist)|William Barlow]] and H.J. Woods is not given sufficient credit by the authors and is largely missing from the, otherwise full, bibliography.  He praised Shubnikov's book (part 1) as being "very clearly written, well illustrated, and easy to understand", but criticised Belov's papers in part 2 because they "lack a central unifying theme."<ref name=Buerger>{{cite journal

==Influence==

In later reviews of the literature by [[Rolph Ludwig Edward Schwarzenberger|R.L.E. Schwarzenberger]]<ref name=Schwarzenberger>{{cite journal
	| last1 = Schwarzenberger
	| first1 = R.L.E.
    | author-link = Rolph Ludwig Edward Schwarzenberger
	| date = 1984
    | language = 
	| title = Colour symmetry
	| url = 
	| journal = [[London Mathematical Society#Publications|Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]]
	| volume = 16
	| issue = 3
	| pages = 209–240
    | jstor = 
	| doi = 10.1112/blms/16.3.209
	| access-date =
}}</ref> and by [[Branko Grünbaum]] and [[Geoffrey Colin Shephard|G.C. Shephard]] in their book ''[[Tilings and patterns]]''<ref name=Grünbaum>{{cite book
	| last1 = Grünbaum
	| first1 = Branko
	| last2 = Shephard
	| first2 = G.C.
	| author-link = 
	| date = 1987
	| title = Tilings and patterns
	| url = https://archive.org/details/isbn_0716711931/page/462/mode/2up
    | url-access = registration
	| location = New York
	| publisher = W.H. Freeman
	| pages = 463–470
	| isbn = 978-0-716-71193-3
}}</ref> the work of the Russian color symmetry school led by A.V. Shubnikov and N.V. Belov was put into its proper historical context. Schwarzenberger, and Grünbaum and Shephard, give credit to Shubnikov and Belov for relaunching the field of color symmetry after the work of [[Heinrich Heesch]] and H.J. Woods in the 1930s was largely ignored. However, they criticise Shubnikov and Belov for taking a crystallographic rather than a group-theoretic approach, and for using their own confusing notation rather than adopting the international standard [[Hermann–Mauguin notation]] for crystallographic symmetry elements.
